_comment: Household electric-vehicle (EV) defaults for occupancy.core.ev. Deliberately kept OUT of equipment.json: an EV is not an hourly-triggered appliance but a stateful battery whose charging depends on trips, state of charge and plug-in behaviour, and its charging power is NOT an internal heat gain (the charger/car sit in a driveway or garage), so it must never enter total_power_kwh / buem's elecLoad. Every key can be overridden per call (EVConfig.with_overrides / load_ev_config) -- e.g. with survey-derived distributions -- without editing this file. Keys starting with '_' are documentation. See docs/ev/design.md for the method and every source.
_ownership_source: Community-analysis default, user-specified for Loenen (Gelderland, NL) on 2026-11-23: EV ownership there is above the national average. For comparison, CBS (2025) 'Meer dan 1 miljoen stekkerauto's in Nederland' reports ~6% of NL private passenger cars as plug-in (a share of cars, not of households). Only used when has_ev is None (unknown, e.g. community analysis); an individual-household run defaults to has_ev=True.
_has_home_charger_note: false = the household owns an EV but has no private charge point (street parking): every kWh is then charged away from home and the household meter sees no EV load.
_home_charging_start_hour_note: null = charging starts as soon as the car is plugged in (uncontrolled charging, the default). A clock hour (e.g. 23 or 21.5) = a charging timer: the car stays connected from plug-in but only starts charging at the next occurrence of that hour, e.g. the start of a Dutch off-peak (dal) tariff. This is the simple 'scheduled' baseline between uncontrolled and optimised (smart) charging. Hours of day assume the profile starts at 00:00 local time.

slow._source: power_kw 7.4 = single-phase 32 A home wallbox, user-specified default (any value may be passed; charging durations follow from energy / power). efficiency 0.92 = 95% inverter/transformer x 97% battery input, as used by Brady & O'Mahony (2016, Sustainable Cities and Society 26:203-216, Sec. 4.3, after Keane & Flynn 2012). taper_* (constant-current/constant-voltage slow-down near full) are estimated, unsourced -- AC charging at <= 11 kW tapers only close to 100%.

fast._source: power_kw 50 = common public DC fast-charger rating; efficiency and taper_* are estimated, unsourced (typical CC-CV behaviour: DC fast charging slows sharply above ~80% SOC). Fast charging's higher battery wear is a technology (degradation) property and is modelled in conversion-technologies, not here; occupancy reports the energy charged per mode so it can be computed.

vehicle._source: battery_capacity_kwh 60 (usable) is estimated, unsourced: Dutch consumer tests of 2024 models span ~51-95 kWh net (id.nl Verbruiksmonitor). consumption_kwh_per_km 0.18 (battery side, real-world) is estimated from id.nl real-world tests of 2024 models (16.8-19.5 kWh/100 km) and the 15-18 kWh/100 km mixed-driving range plus 20-30% real-world uplift cited by consumer guides; Brady & O'Mahony (2016) measured 0.265 kWh/km for the 2010-era Mitsubishi i-MiEV. max_ac/max_dc_power_kw are the car's on-board limits (estimated): effective charging power = min(charger, car). monthly_consumption_multiplier is a hook for winter consumption uplift (cabin heating, cold battery); left neutral (1.0) because no NL-sourced monthly profile has been found yet.

battery._source: Estimated, unsourced. soc_target_home 0.9 reflects the common practice of capping daily home charging below 100% for battery health (set 1.0 to charge to full). soc_min is the reserve the driver never runs below: a trip that would cross it is assumed to include an away (fast) top-up. soc_initial only seeds the warm-up period (simulation.warmup_days), so it barely affects the result -- the same reason Brady & O'Mahony (2016) simulate two days and keep the second.

mobility._annual_km_source: CBS: a privately owned electric passenger car drove on average 14.8 thousand km in 2023 (CBS news 2024/45 'Zakelijke automobilist rijdt meer elektrisch dan op diesel'; all EVs incl. business: 18.1 thousand km in 2024, provisional). The lognormal daily-distance scale is derived from this so the expected annual mileage matches it; presence coupling can only lower the realised value (see docs/ev/design.md).
mobility._use_probability_source: Estimated, unsourced: probability that the car is driven on a given day.
mobility._hour_weights_source: Relative weights per hour of day (index 0 = 00:00-01:00), normalised in code, so raw survey counts can be pasted in directly. weekday departure = first departure from home, digitised approximately from Brady & O'Mahony (2016) Fig. 3 (Irish EV trial, 15 cars, 4021 weekday driving days); weekday arrival = 'expected' arrival-home counts digitised approximately from their Fig. 10. Weekend arrays are estimated, unsourced (the trial covered weekdays only). Irish 2010s data, not Dutch: replace with Loenen survey data when available.
mobility._distance_source: Daily driven distance is lognormal; sigma 0.8 is estimated to match the shape of Brady & O'Mahony (2016) Fig. 3 (mode within 1-40 km, long tail past 100 km). Its scale is derived from annual_km, not set here.
mobility._copula_source: Gaussian-copula correlation between (departure time, arrival time, daily distance), the dependence-modelling approach of Lojowska, Kurowicka, Papaefthymiou & van der Sluis (2012, IEEE Trans. Power Systems 27:1960-1968) for Dutch EV demand. departure-distance -0.37 is Brady & O'Mahony's (2016) measured Pearson correlation (R(1,3)); the two arrival correlations are estimated, unsourced. Must be positive definite.
mobility._presence_coupling_note: Ties the car to the occupancy profile: a trip window is accepted when at least min_absent_fraction of its hours have someone out of the house (n_present < num_persons). Up to max_draws candidate trips are drawn per day; if none satisfies it the best one is kept, and if nobody is ever out the car stays home that day. This repo's own design, not from the literature.

plug_in._model_source: model = 'soc_table' (default): the step table above. model = 'logistic': connection probability 1 / (1 + exp((SOC - indifference_soc) / sensitivity_soc)), the univariate logit connection model of Harbrecht, McKenna, Fischer & Fichtner (2018, KIT IIP Working Paper 29, Sec. 4.2.2) and Fischer, Harbrecht, Surmann & McKenna (2019, Applied Energy 233-234:644-658). sensitivity_soc 0.0782 = sigma * sqrt(3) / pi with sigma = 14.2 %-SOC, the standard deviation of SOC at plug-in measured in three German EV fleet trials (Schaeuble et al. 2017, J. Clean. Prod. 150). indifference_soc 0.5 is their home-charging value that matched the private-household MINI E trial (0.42 vs 0.40 charging events per vehicle-day); German, 2010s data.
plug_in._source: probability = chance of plugging in at home on arrival, by arrival SOC (bin i covers SOC up to soc_bin_upper_edges[i]); estimated, unsourced, shaped after Brady & O'Mahony's (2016) SOC-conditioned charging decision (overall P(charge overnight | charger available) = 0.55) and Lojowska et al.'s SOC < 50% scenario. Plug-in delay after arrival: ~70% immediately, ~30% spread uniformly between 15 min and 5 h, read from Brady & O'Mahony (2016) Fig. 7. evening_check_hour: on a day the car stays home unplugged, the plug-in decision is re-taken at this hour (estimated).

away_charging._source: Opportunistic charging away from home (workplace, public, fast charger), on top of the forced top-up when a trip would cross soc_min. Calibrated (0.27, checked over 90 simulated generic/working_couple/family_with_children households: mean home share 0.80-0.84 for 0.28-0.22) so roughly a fifth of charged energy comes from away from home: RVO Nationaal Laadonderzoek 2025 reports EV drivers who can charge at home charge 81% of their kilometres there (6% at work, 5% public). Charged with away_charging_mode; this energy is NOT on the household meter.
